source: Wang et al. (2023) Plan-and-Solve Prompting
finding: Asking GPT-3 to first devise a plan, then carry it out, beats plain 'think step by step'. Adding detail (extract variables, calculate intermediate results) helps more. This is Polya 'devise a plan' turned into a prompt.
numbers: PS+ beats Zero-shot-CoT by at least 5 points on every arithmetic set except GSM8K (+2.9). PS alone averages +2.5 points. Average over arithmetic sets: PS+ 76.7%, 8-shot manual CoT 77.6%, Auto-CoT 75.9%. Symbolic: Last Letters 75.2% vs 65.2%; Coin Flip 99.6% vs 96.8%. Commonsense: CSQA 71.9 vs 65.2; StrategyQA 65.4 vs 63.8.
limits: GPT-3 (text-davinci-003) only, greedy decoding; gain is smallest on the hardest set (GSM8K). Old model; later models already plan by default.
agent_relevance: A planning instruction is cheap and gives a few points on weak models. It is a prompt-level heuristic, not a control layer.

source: Wang et al. (2023) Plan-and-Solve Prompting (error analysis)
finding: Error analysis on GSM8K shows what the planning heuristic fixes: missing-step and calculation errors, not misunderstanding of the problem.
numbers: 100 sampled problems: Zero-shot-CoT errors were 7% calculation, 12% missing step, 27% semantic misunderstanding. Failed problems among the sample: CoT 46, PS 43, PS+ 39. PS+ error rates: calculation 5%, missing step 7%, semantic about equal to CoT. Having a variable list and a plan correlates negatively with both error types.
limits: Small sample (100 problems; 46/43/39 failures); correlational, not causal.
agent_relevance: Heuristics help execution slips; they do not fix a wrong problem representation. The control layer must still check understanding early.

source: Wang et al. (2023) Plan-and-Solve Prompting (self-consistency)
finding: Plan-and-solve stacks with voting. Heuristic and sampling gains are additive.
numbers: GSM8K: PS+ 58.7% -> 73.7% with self-consistency (N=10, T=0.7); SVAMP 75.7% -> 84.4%. Zero-shot-CoT with SC: 70.7% (GSM8K), 81.7% (SVAMP).
limits: Single model, 10 samples.
agent_relevance: A heuristic prompt plus independent sampling is a safe combination.

source: Kojima et al. (2022) Large Language Models are Zero-Shot Reasoners
finding: A single generic trigger phrase ('Let's think step by step') lifts reasoning a lot with no examples. The simplest 'teach a heuristic' result.
numbers: text-davinci-002: MultiArith 17.7% -> 78.7%; GSM8K 10.4% -> 40.7%. Zero-shot-CoT still below hand-written few-shot CoT.
quote: Zero-shot-CoT substantially outperforms four out of six arithmetic reasoning tasks
limits: Large gains on four of six arithmetic sets, symbolic and some logic tasks; not on all. Model-scale dependent.
agent_relevance: Baseline for all heuristic prompts. Any scaffold must beat this trigger, not beat nothing.

source: Zhou et al. (2023) Least-to-Most Prompting Enables Complex Reasoning in Large Language Models
finding: Decompose into easier subproblems, solve in order (Polya 'solve a simpler related problem'). It generalizes to problems harder than the examples shown, where CoT fails.
numbers: SCAN length split, code-davinci-002: least-to-most 99.7% vs CoT 16.2%. Last-letter concatenation: L=4 94.0% vs CoT 84.2%; standard prompting 0%. 500 lists per length.
limits: Needs task-specific prompts; authors say decomposition does not generalize across domains even inside GSM8K. Gains are largest where decomposition is easy to write.
agent_relevance: Decomposition operator is strong when the decomposition is well specified; weak when the model must invent it.

source: Zhou et al. (2023) Least-to-Most (GSM8K breakdown)
finding: On GSM8K the gain is small overall but grows with the number of steps. Transfer from a 2-step demo to harder problems is real but modest.
numbers: 1-shot GSM8K, code-davinci-002: least-to-most 62.39% vs CoT 60.87% overall. By steps: 2 steps 74.53 vs 76.68 (worse); 3: 68.91 vs 67.29; 4: 59.73 vs 59.39; 5+: 45.23 vs 39.07.
quote: nearly all problems in GSM8K can be accurately solved if the large language models are provided with the correct decomposition
limits: Single prompt; one model; differences at 2-4 steps are small.
agent_relevance: Decomposition helps only where problems exceed what the model handles in one pass. Gate it by difficulty.

source: Zheng et al. (2024) Take a Step Back: Evoking Reasoning via Abstraction
finding: Step-back asks the model to first state the general principle or concept, then solve. It is a computational version of Polya 'look for a more general problem'. It beats CoT and 'take a deep breath' on science QA.
numbers: PaLM-2L: MMLU Physics 66.4% -> 73.2% (+7), Chemistry 70.9% -> 81.8% (+11), TimeQA +27 (Step-Back+RAG 68.7% vs GPT-4 45.6%), MuSiQue +7. Averages over 5 runs. Fixes 20.5% of baseline errors on Physics, introduces 11.9% new ones. TimeQA Hard: 62.3% vs 42.6% GPT-4.
limits: Few-shot demonstrations of abstraction used; on TimeQA gain depends on RAG. Over 90% of remaining errors are in the reasoning step, not the abstraction step.
agent_relevance: Abstraction is easy to teach (robust to number of exemplars); execution remains the bottleneck. A principle-first step is cheap to add.

source: Zheng et al. (2024) Step-Back (cross-model and generic-prompt controls)
finding: Zero-shot CoT and 'take a deep breath' did not help on knowledge tasks where step-back did. Gains hold across model families but vary.
numbers: TimeQA: CoT and TDB show no improvement over baseline (about 40-42% for PaLM-2L). MMLU Physics: GPT-4 69.4% -> 84.5%; Llama2-70B 51.9% -> 64.8%. MuSiQue: PaLM-2L 35.5% -> 42.8%.
limits: Pairings of numbers to columns read from text extraction of tables; treat as approximate.
agent_relevance: Generic 'think harder' phrases are not the same as a targeted heuristic. Test each heuristic against its generic control.

source: Yasunaga et al. (2024) Large Language Models as Analogical Reasoners
finding: Model is asked to recall related problems (Polya 'have you seen a related problem?') and then solve. Self-generated exemplars match or slightly beat hand-picked few-shot CoT.
numbers: GSM8K GPT-3.5-turbo: 0-shot 75.0, 0-CoT 75.8, 5-shot CoT 76.7, self-generated exemplars 77.8. MATH GPT-3.5-turbo: roughly 37% vs about 35% for 5-shot CoT (table text garbled).
limits: Gains small on GSM8K, larger on MATH and Codeforces. Works better with bigger models.
agent_relevance: Self-recall of related problems is a usable operator, but quality depends on the recalled exemplars being right.

source: Yasunaga et al. (2024) Analogical prompting (failure audit)
finding: The authors hand-audited why recall works or fails. Wrong or irrelevant recalled problems are common; a generalization gap is the biggest single cause among relevant correct recalls.
numbers: 50 correct + 50 incorrect (GSM8K+MATH). Correct: 35 relevant and correct exemplars, 9 relevant but wrong, 6 irrelevant. Incorrect: 28 relevant and correct yet still failed (12 generalization gap, 8 over-reliance on exemplar, 8 other), 12 relevant but wrong, 10 irrelevant.
limits: Manual audit, 100 items. Smaller models did better with retrieved exemplars than self-generated.
agent_relevance: Recalling a solved relative does not guarantee transfer. Add a check that the relative really matches (the human transfer problem again).

source: Suzgun & Kalai (2024) Meta-Prompting: Task-Agnostic Scaffolding
finding: One GPT-4 acts as conductor: splits the task, calls expert copies of itself, verifies, and may run Python. A control layer built from prompts alone.
numbers: Averaged over tasks, meta-prompting with Python beats standard prompting by 17.1%, dynamic expert prompting by 17.3%, multi-persona by 15.2%. Game of 24: +56.0 points from adding Python to meta-prompting. Checkmate-in-One +20.8% even without Python. Sonnet writing: standard prompting 62%.
limits: GPT-4 only; much of the gain comes from the Python tool; little gain on MGSM and Geometric Shapes except 4-6 points in low-resource languages; many calls.
agent_relevance: Evidence that a conductor loop with verification helps on trial-and-error tasks, and that tools carry much of the gain.

source: Zhou et al. (2024) Self-Discover: LLMs Self-Compose Reasoning Structures
finding: Model picks from a menu of reasoning modules (break into subtasks, critical thinking, step-by-step), adapts them to the task, and writes a reasoning plan used for every instance of that task. A self-built Polya heuristic list. Beats CoT and plan-and-solve.
numbers: PaLM 2-L: BBH 56 (direct) / 60 (CoT) / 61 (PS) / 67 (Self-Discover); T4D 30/40/42/69; MATH 45/42/49/50.5. GPT-4: BBH 58/75/73/81; T4D 51/52/53/85; MATH 70.5/71/70/73. Beats CoT on 21 of 25 tasks. 10-40x fewer calls than self-consistency.
limits: Gain on MATH is small (1-7 points PaLM, 2-3 GPT-4). Of MATH failures 74.7% are computation errors; structures themselves correct 87.5% of the time. Best on world-knowledge tasks, moderate on algorithmic.
agent_relevance: Task-level heuristic selection is cheap (3 extra calls per task). It improves structure but not arithmetic, so pair with a checker or tool.

source: Zhou et al. (2024) Self-Discover (transfer of structures across models)
finding: Reasoning structures written by one model transfer to other models, so a heuristic plan acts as portable knowledge.
numbers: Structures found by PaLM 2-L applied to GPT-4 (four tasks), and GPT-4 structures applied to Llama2-70B and ChatGPT, improved over CoT and over OPRO-optimized prompts on the tested tasks.
limits: Few tasks in the first transfer; exact deltas not recorded here.
agent_relevance: A stored task-level plan can be reused across model versions.

source: Yang et al. (2024) Buffer of Thoughts (NeurIPS)
finding: A growing library of high-level thought templates distilled from solved problems; retrieve one, instantiate it. An LLM version of schema and heuristic teaching with a memory.
numbers: GPT-4 on Game of 24: 3.0% base, 11.0% CoT, 74.0% ToT, 82.4% BoT. Versus meta-prompting: +23 Game of 24, +20 Geometric Shapes, +51 Checkmate-in-One. Cost about 12% of multi-query methods like ToT. Llama3-8B + BoT can approach or pass plain Llama3-70B on some tasks.
limits: Template quality depends on the base model that distills them; removing the problem-distiller hurts hard tasks; tasks are partly template-friendly (Game of 24, chess).
agent_relevance: Reusable strategy templates with retrieval is the closest LLM analogue of teaching heuristics for transfer. Test on novel task families.

source: Gandhi et al. (2025) Cognitive Behaviors that Enable Self-Improving Reasoners
finding: Four human problem-solving behaviours (verification, backtracking, subgoal setting, backward chaining) decide whether RL helps a model. Priming a weak model with them closes the gap to a strong model.
numbers: Countdown, same RL: Qwen-2.5-3B reaches about 60%, Llama-3.2-3B about 30%. Priming Llama with behaviour-rich traces matches or exceeds Qwen. Empty chain-of-thought or filler tokens: 30-35%, same as base. Priming with incorrect solutions that still show the behaviours performs about the same as correct ones.
limits: Training-based, not prompting; one task (Countdown) plus transfer checks; 3B models.
agent_relevance: Strongest recent evidence that the behaviours, not correctness, carry the effect. For a scaffold: demand these behaviours explicitly, and do not rely on extra tokens alone.

source: Gandhi et al. (2025) Cognitive Behaviors (transfer to MATH/GPQA, pretraining data)
finding: Countdown-trained behaviours showed up on other tasks, and behaviour-rich pretraining text mattered.
numbers: Qwen RL-tuned on Countdown: on MATH backtracking frequency 0.15 -> 0.59, verification 0.02 -> 0.29; MATH accuracy 38% -> 50% with their prompt format (4-shot 44% -> zero-shot 50% in Qwen's format). 200 questions each from GPQA and MATH. Continued pretraining on 8.3M tokens of behaviour-rich OpenWebMath rewrites helped Llama; a control set with few behaviours did not.
limits: 200 questions per set, so wide error bars; behaviours counted by an LLM classifier.
agent_relevance: Behaviours generalize across math-like domains in this model; it does not prove human-style heuristic transfer.

source: Didolkar et al. (2024) Metacognitive Capabilities of LLMs: Mathematical Problem Solving
finding: GPT-4 labels math questions with skills, clusters them, and at test time names the needed skill and gets examples of that skill. A model-made heuristic index beats fixed or random examples.
numbers: GSM8K GPT-4-0613: CoT 93.00, random-exemplar 92.87, skill-based 94.31, skill-based maj@5 95.38. GPT-3.5-Turbo: skill-based 82.03 vs retrieval-RSD 76.8. MATH with PAL: +7.52% over 4-shot PAL using one code example plus three skill examples (500-item subset).
limits: Ceiling effect on GSM8K (+1.3); gains are on harder MATH topics; labels from GPT-4 only.
agent_relevance: Skill-keyed example retrieval is a cheap way to choose which heuristic to apply. Random exemplars give no gain, which isolates the matching step.

source: Huang et al. (2024) Large Language Models Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet
finding: Telling a model to review and fix its own answer (Polya 'look back') does not help without outside feedback; it often hurts. Earlier positive results used the correct label to decide when to stop.
numbers: GSM8K GPT-3.5: 75.9 (standard) -> 75.1 (1 round) -> 74.7 (2 rounds). GPT-4: 95.5 -> 91.5 -> 89.0. CommonSenseQA GPT-3.5: 75.8 -> 38.1 -> 41.8. With oracle labels GSM8K GPT-3.5: 75.9 -> 84.3; GPT-4 95.5 -> 97.5. GPT-3.5 keeps its answer 74.7% of the time and more often turns right into wrong than the reverse.
limits: Intrinsic self-correction only; 2023 models; later RL-trained reasoning models show some self-checking.
agent_relevance: Do not rely on a plain 'check your work' step. The reflection step needs an external signal (tool, tests, second solver).

source: Huang et al. (2024) Self-Correct paper: multi-agent debate control
finding: Re-running multi-agent debate on the full GSM8K test set (not 100 items) with the original prompt, the debate gain is no better than self-consistency at equal numbers of responses.
numbers: Debate with 3 agents and 2 rounds on gpt-3.5-turbo-0301 vs self-consistency with the same number of responses; debate did not beat self-consistency (exact figures not extracted).
limits: Single dataset; one model version.
agent_relevance: Compare any multi-pass scaffold against equal-compute voting before crediting the heuristic.

source: Zhou et al. (2022) Teaching Algorithmic Reasoning via In-context Learning
finding: Teaching an explicit algorithm as a skill, with every step spelled out, gives near-perfect and length-generalizing arithmetic. Vague rationales (CoT) do not generalize.
numbers: code-davinci-002: error reduction of about 10x (parity), 9x (addition), 5x (multiplication), 2x (subtraction) against best baselines. Addition near perfect out of distribution; few-shot, CoT, scratchpad and instruction-only fall off with length.
limits: Works for fully specified algorithms, not open-ended heuristics; long prompts; skills can interfere when mixed.
agent_relevance: Boundary condition: precise procedures transfer, loose heuristics are the hard case Schoenfeld described.

source: Kramer & Baumann (2024) Cognitive Prompting
finding: A fixed or self-chosen sequence of cognitive operations (clarify goal, decompose, filter, abstract, pattern-recognize) beats plain answering on GSM8K for several open models. A hybrid reusing own correct solutions as few-shot examples is best.
numbers: GSM8K, 3 repetitions, six open models (LLaMA 8B/70B, Gemma 9B/27B, Qwen 7B/32B): hybrid variant reaches about 95% on LLaMA 70B. Deterministic, self-adaptive and hybrid all above zero-shot in the figures.
limits: Small workshop-style paper; exact per-model numbers only in figures; GSM8K is near saturation; no comparison to plain CoT read.
agent_relevance: Supports choosing operations from a menu. Without a CoT control the gain cannot be credited to the heuristics specifically.

source: DeepSeek-AI (2025) DeepSeek-R1
finding: RL on verifiable rewards makes reflection, re-checking and trying alternatives appear on their own, without teaching heuristics. Hand-written human reasoning in SFT may limit exploration.
numbers: R1-Zero shows rising reasoning length and an 'aha moment' with re-evaluation ('Wait, wait.'). The paper reports few-shot prompting consistently degrades R1 and recommends zero-shot with a stated output format.
limits: Qualitative evidence for the 'aha' part; no clean causal test in the text read.
agent_relevance: For strong reasoning models, extra heuristic prompts can hurt. Test the scaffold per model; fewer instructions may be better.

source: Lenat (1983) EURISKO: a program that learns new heuristics
finding: Older AI system that represented heuristics as objects and evolved new heuristics for a domain. Early computational study of discovering and teaching heuristics.
numbers: Not opened this session; no figures recorded.
limits: Not read; recalled from memory, verify before citing.
agent_relevance: Heuristics as editable, scored objects is the idea behind stored templates (BoT) and self-discovered modules.

source: Newell & Simon (1972) Human Problem Solving (GPS, means-ends analysis)
finding: The General Problem Solver put one general heuristic, means-ends analysis, in a program. Base of the Polya-to-AI lineage.
numbers: Not opened; no figures.
limits: Background only; not read this session.
agent_relevance: Control strategy separate from domain knowledge is the architecture our scaffold copies.

source: Wei et al. (2022) Chain-of-Thought Prompting Elicits Reasoning in Large Language Models
finding: Foundational few-shot CoT paper; downloaded but not read closely this session.
numbers: Not extracted.
limits: Not read.
agent_relevance: Cite as the base technique that the heuristic prompts above are compared against.
